title: Predicate type mismatches can yield false PASS
description:
SAFETY BUG. portable_row.rs currently treats unlike scalar types as ordinary non-equality: values_equal returns false, ordered comparisons return None and therefore false, and ne or surrounding not can turn the same authoring mistake into PASS. Verified example: a numeric cell compared with the string literal "0" does not refuse, so type mistakes can silently invert constraint meaning.

Pin a no-implicit-coercion comparison contract for existing predicates before cross-binding DuckDB evaluation is added. Number/number, string/string, and boolean/boolean comparisons retain their declared semantics. Incomparable operand categories must stop the whole evaluation with a typed refusal carrying rule/operator/type and available localization context; they must never become an ordinary predicate verdict. Null comparison and membership behavior must be explicitly covered rather than inherited accidentally.

This is independent of binding-qualified references. bd-3is depends on it so the DuckDB lane cannot acquire different coercion semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. eq, ne, gt, gte, lt, lte, and in refuse on incompatible scalar categories instead of returning true or false; tests include numeric 0 versus string "0" and negated/NE forms that currently risk false PASS.
2. Valid number/number, string/string, and boolean/boolean comparisons keep existing behavior, including deterministic numeric comparison across JSON number representations.
3. Null-versus-null and null-versus-present semantics are explicitly pinned in docs/plan.md and tests; no implicit string/number/boolean coercion is introduced.
4. Batch and embedded portable execution emit the same refusal code and stable detail for the same constraint and relation, including rule_id, operator, operand categories, and available binding/key/field context.
5. The batch-only cross-binding evaluator in bd-3is reuses this semantic contract and does not delegate coercion decisions to DuckDB.
notes: Primary files: crates/verify-engine/src/portable_row.rs, refusal mapping in crates/verify-engine/src/embedded.rs and crates/verify-cli/src/run.rs, plus focused parity/refusal tests. Use E_BAD_EXPR only if the plan explicitly defines it for runtime incomparability; otherwise amend the refusal table before adding a code.
close_reason: Implemented type-strict predicate comparisons with localized E_BAD_EXPR refusals in batch and embedded execution, explicit null semantics, and regression coverage; required functional gates pass.

title: Lock down DuckDB external I/O and reject non-read-only SQL in query_zero_rows
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `crates/verify-duckdb/src/lib.rs:54-66` opens an in-memory DuckDB connection and registers `--bind` inputs without locking down external I/O (`SET enable_external_access = false; SET lock_configuration = true;`).
- `crates/verify-duckdb/src/query_rules.rs:167-172` executes arbitrary SQL strings from rule files against that connection.

## Risk
`verify` is an authorized tool in `veil` boundaries. An agent-authored or untrusted rule file can invoke `read_csv_auto('/protected/...')`, `read_parquet(...)`, `ATTACH`, or `COPY (...) TO '/tmp/exfil'` to read arbitrary host files or exfiltrate bound datasets outside the `veil` boundary.

## Fix
1. Immediately after loading all `--bind` inputs into DuckDB, execute:
   - `SET autoinstall_known_extensions = false;`
   - `SET autoload_known_extensions = false;`
   - `SET enable_external_access = false;`
   - `SET lock_configuration = true;`
2. Enforce read-only SQL validation on `query_zero_rows` (reject DDL/DML/`COPY`/`ATTACH`/`DETACH`/`PRAGMA`/`LOAD`/`INSTALL`/`SET`).
acceptance_criteria:
- DuckDB connection disables external access, extension autoload/autoinstall, and locks configuration right after registering `--bind` inputs.
- `query_zero_rows` rejects non-read-only statements deterministically before/at execution.
- Regression tests verify that rules attempting `read_csv_auto`, `COPY (...) TO`, `ATTACH`, and `SET enable_external_access = true` fail cleanly.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator on an exact git-archive export of 02376f5 (the committed HEAD that includes 57a5d98 and the later q4d commit; NOT the live tree, which Lane B is editing), built against the pane's target dir so DuckDB was reused, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3. Suites: cargo test -p verify-duckdb = 59 unit + 3 lock_integration + 7 query_rules passed; cargo test -p verify-cli --test cli (36) --test portable_rules (10) --test refusals (8) --test determinism (2) --test binding_qualified_predicates (5) --test binding_qualified_refusals (5) --test binding_qualified_determinism (3) all passed; 0 ignored. Independent hostile checks with MY OWN payloads through a snapshot of the built binary (verify run c.json --bind property=<csv> --json --no-witness): REFUSED exit 2 with typed codes and no file read or written: glob('/etc/*'), read_text('/etc/hosts'), getenv('HOME'), PRAGMA database_list, INSTALL httpfs, a UNION ALL embedding read_json('/etc/hosts'), case-mangled sElEcT..ReAd_CsV_aUtO, a subquery EXISTS(...read_csv_auto), FROM '/etc/hosts' with tab/newline whitespace, unparenthesized COPY property TO <path>, EXPORT DATABASE <dir> (all E_BAD_CONSTRAINTS); no /etc/hosts content (127.0.0.1/localhost) in any output; the COPY target file and the EXPORT directory were NOT created; legitimate control rule (SELECT ... WHERE property_id IS NULL) => exit 0 PASS. Two EVASION payloads slipped past the lexical validator by design (it skips quoted identifiers and comments): SELECT * FROM "read_csv"('/etc/hosts') and SELECT * FROM read_csv /* x */ ('/etc/hosts'): both were still STOPPED at execution by the locked connection (E_SQL_ERROR, exit 2, error text redacted by default, no leak), which is the defense-in-depth second line the pane described and the direct evidence that the lockdown works. Diff scan: no removed assertions, no #[ignore] in the 16h commit. title: Compile and validate binding-qualified predicates
description:
AUTHORING AND STATIC VALIDATION lane for binding-qualified predicates.

## Background
Once the protocol types exist, structured JSON/YAML authoring must be able to express cross-binding comparisons without admitting raw SQL. The predicate check binding remains the anchor. An omitted ColumnReference.binding resolves to the anchor; an explicit distinct binding makes the compiled rule batch_only.

The compiler and validator must derive this property from the complete expression tree. Operators cannot override semantics by declaring contradictory portability, and malformed key alignment must be rejected before any input is loaded.

## Scope
Extend the existing structured authoring compiler and compiled-artifact validator. Reuse the pure analysis surface from the protocol foundation so compile, validate, and later run ingestion cannot drift.

## Boundaries
Do not implement DuckDB execution, SQL lowering, CLI run routing, report construction, embedded lowering, scoring, or new predicate operators. SQL authoring remains exclusively for query_zero_rows.
design:
## Exact file ownership
- crates/verify-cli/src/compile/portable.rs
- crates/verify-cli/src/compile/mod.rs
- crates/verify-cli/src/validate.rs
- fixtures/authoring/binding_qualified/maturity_date_immutable.yaml (new)

## Technical approach
1. Parse optional binding fields through the shared predicate types; keep deny_unknown_fields and scalar-only literal safety intact.
2. Represent authored key_fields as Option<Vec<String>> until validation so an omitted declaration and an explicit empty list produce their distinct stable reasons; only normalize to the compiled Binding after validation.
3. After normalizing predicate aliases, recursively analyze the expression using verify-core.
4. Infer portability rather than defaulting every structured rule to portable. If authoring omits portability, emit the derived value. If it declares portability, require exact agreement.
5. Validate that the anchor and every resolved reference are declared. For binding-qualified predicates, validate non-empty participant key_fields and equal positional arity.
6. Map authoring defects to E_BAD_AUTHORING with stable reason values and rule/binding/key detail. Compiled-artifact validation must reject the same defects as invalid constraints.
7. Preserve the existing no-output-on-compile-error guarantee.
8. Keep existing single-binding authoring byte-compatible and portable.

Compiler errors must remain deterministic regardless of map iteration order; use the ordered analysis output from verify-core.
acceptance_criteria:
1. JSON and YAML authoring compile a binding-qualified predicate into one verify.constraint.v1 rule with optional column-reference bindings preserved and portability=batch_only.
2. Existing single-binding predicates compile byte-identically with portability=portable, including an explicit reference equal to the anchor.
3. Omitted portability is inferred; explicit correct portability is accepted; explicit portable on a cross-binding expression and explicit batch_only on an anchor-only expression both refuse with E_BAD_AUTHORING and reason=portability_mismatch.
4. Recursive references in every predicate form are checked; an undeclared nested binding refuses with reason=undeclared_reference.
5. Missing, explicitly empty, or unequal-arity participant key_fields refuse authoring with the pinned reason and actionable detail.
6. verify validate accepts the good compiled fixture and rejects equivalent malformed compiled artifacts through the shared core validator.
7. A failed compile writes no output artifact.
8. query_zero_rows remains unavailable through structured authoring and SQL authoring behavior is unchanged.
9. Focused unit tests cover successful compilation, legacy compatibility, both portability mismatches, undeclared references, every key-shape defect, and no-output behavior.

## Test plan

- Compile command test in mod.rs proving a malformed cross-binding source writes no artifact.
- Validator tests in validate.rs for valid and malformed compiled artifacts.
- Compile the new authoring fixture twice and compare output bytes for determinism.
- Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and ubs --diff.

## Coordination

title: Execute binding-qualified predicates in DuckDB
description:
DUCKDB EXECUTION lane for binding-qualified predicates.

## Background
All batch bindings already coexist as temporary relations in one verify_duckdb::BatchContext. This lane evaluates the existing structured predicate AST across those relations. Operators still author structured predicates, never SQL. Check::Predicate.binding is the anchor; each distinct referenced binding contributes exactly one row through positionally aligned key_fields.

The implementation must preserve portable scalar semantics and must not let DuckDB implicit casts, collation, or scan order determine truth or refusal behavior.

## Row and key contract
- Evaluate every anchor row exactly once.
- Non-anchor-only rows are outside the invocation.
- Validate all participant key fields before verdicts.
- Keys are ordered tagged scalar tuples; physical field names may differ by position.
- Null/non-scalar/unrepresentable/type-incompatible keys refuse E_KEY_INVALID.
- Duplicate tuples anywhere in a participant refuse E_KEY_AMBIGUOUS.
- Missing anchor counterparts refuse E_KEY_UNMATCHED.
- Missing fields refuse E_FIELD_NOT_FOUND; incomparable predicate operands refuse E_BAD_EXPR.
- False predicates produce one affected anchor entry; field/value appear only for one unambiguous anchor column.

## Boundaries
Do not change authoring, CLI routing, report rendering, README/AGENTS, embedded portability, policy, scoring, or add raw SQL to artifacts.
design:
## Exact file ownership
- crates/verify-engine/src/lib.rs
- crates/verify-engine/src/scalar.rs (new)
- crates/verify-engine/src/portable_row.rs
- crates/verify-duckdb/src/lib.rs
- crates/verify-duckdb/src/bindings.rs
- crates/verify-duckdb/src/scalar.rs (new)
- crates/verify-duckdb/src/binding_predicates.rs (new)

## Technical approach
1. Extract the pure scalar category/comparison truth table from portable_row.rs into verify-engine::scalar without changing portable behavior. Cover eq/ne/ordering/in, null semantics, and every incompatible pair.
2. Centralize DuckDB Value to protocol scalar conversion below the CLI in verify-duckdb::scalar. Both batch portable materialization and the new executor must consume this converter after CLI integration.
3. Add BindingRegistry metadata/query helpers needed for deterministic field preflight and quoted relation/column access.
4. Build a dedicated batch predicate executor accepting Rule, Connection, and BindingRegistry. It validates declared fields, key usability, tuple category compatibility, and full-relation uniqueness before evaluation.
5. Lower the structured AST deterministically. Quote validated identifiers and bind or canonically render literals. Join each distinct non-anchor binding to the anchor once using positional key equality.
6. Never issue one query per anchor row and never cross join then filter. Execution stays set-oriented.
7. Evaluate every boolean branch for comparability even if a truth verdict could short-circuit.
8. Sort validation candidates, first refusal, and affected entries through canonical protocol ordering rather than DuckDB scan order.
9. Return typed executor errors with the exact detail required for E_KEY_INVALID, E_KEY_AMBIGUOUS, E_KEY_UNMATCHED, E_FIELD_NOT_FOUND, and E_BAD_EXPR. Do not construct the top-level VerifyReport here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Portable-row scalar tests continue to pass unchanged after semantic extraction, and the shared truth table covers all scalar category pairs and null behavior.
2. DuckDB scalar conversion has one implementation below the CLI and either produces the same protocol Value used by portable evaluation or a typed unrepresentable-value error.
3. Full structured predicate grammar passes and fails correctly with binding-qualified operands, including nested boolean forms, membership, is_null, and is_blank; at least one case references two distinct non-anchor bindings and proves each is joined once.
4. Composite keys with different physical names align positionally and use exact string/type-strict scalar identity.
5. Missing/empty/incompatible key metadata is rejected by protocol validation; runtime invalid, duplicate, and unmatched keys return the pinned typed errors and stable detail.
6. All referenced fields are preflighted before row verdicts; missing and incomparable operands cannot become PASS or FAIL.
7. Each failed anchor row yields one deterministically ordered affected entry. Non-anchor-only rows do not affect violation_count.
8. Duplicate keys in non-anchor-only data still refuse because identity is validated over the full participant relation.
9. Equivalent physical row-order permutations produce identical semantic RuleResult or first-refusal detail.
10. The executor reuses the supplied BatchContext connection, performs set-oriented keyed joins, and opens no database or durable state.
11. Unit tests exercise PASS, FAIL, every operator family, composite/different-name keys, every refusal boundary, row-domain asymmetry, localization, and deterministic ordering.
notes:
## Test plan
- verify-engine scalar truth-table and regression tests.
- verify-duckdb unit tests using one in-memory connection and temporary relations.
- Assert generated execution never relies on direct mixed-category DuckDB comparison.
- Include shuffled insertion-order cases and multiple simultaneous defects to prove refusal precedence.
- Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, ubs --diff, and the relevant performance smoke checks.

## Coordination
Depends on bd-3a3. Reserve only the exact files above. It runs in parallel with authoring/validation and must not touch CLI integration files.

Verified with fmt, clippy, 268 workspace tests, diff checks, and zero critical findings across the changed Rust files.

title: REGRESSION 0.5.0: single-binding rules fail to materialize any relation containing a date column
description:
Introduced between 0.4.0 and 0.5.0, almost certainly by 2e92594 'fix: compare temporal binding predicates in DuckDB' (the bd-ch7 fix).

EXACT REPRO — this command returned a correct FAIL on 0.4.0 and errors on 0.5.0:
  verify run cmbs_today.compiled.json --bind new=<absee_tape>.csv
  0.4.0: FAIL SEC_RATE_NONZERO binding=new key.ASSETNUMBER=5-001
  0.5.0: failed to materialize binding new: column FILING_DATE:
         DuckDB date value cannot be represented as a protocol scalar

Minimal repro - a single 'unique' rule on a non-date column also fails:
  rules: [{id: KEY_UNIQUE, binding: tape, op: unique, columns: [ASSETNUMBER]}]
  -> failed to materialize binding tape: column FILING_DATE: ...
FILING_DATE is not referenced by any rule. The whole relation is being
materialized into protocol scalars and the date column aborts the load.

THE TWO LANES HAVE DIVERGED. Same file, same session, verify 0.5.0:
  cross-binding predicate  -> VERIFY PASS   (temporal handled, bd-ch7 fix)
  single-binding unique    -> materialization error on an unreferenced date

So the bd-ch7 fix made temporal comparison work in the NEW path while the
EXISTING path still cannot even load a relation containing a date. That is the
exact drift risk recorded in bd-286 - it has now happened, and in the opposite
direction from the one anticipated.

IMPACT: any single-binding constraint set over real SEC ABS-EE data is dead.
Those tapes carry FILING_DATE, REPORTINGPERIODBEGINNINGDATE,
REPORTINGPERIODENDDATE, MATURITYDATE, ORIGINATIONDATE and more. This blocks
credit-surveillance rules (realized loss, special-servicer transfer,
modification, payment status) which are all single-binding.

EXPECTED: materializing a binding must not fail on a column no rule
references. Either materialize lazily (only referenced columns), or apply the
same DuckDB-native handling the cross-binding path now uses, or represent
temporals as text at load with the no-coercion guarantee enforced at
comparison time instead.

P0 because it is a regression that breaks previously working behaviour on
the primary corpus.
close_reason: Fixed by projecting only the columns portable rules read; attribution corrected to 5531f8e / v0.4.0

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE + FIX.

MECHANISM
crates/verify-cli/src/run.rs materialize_relation ran 'SELECT * FROM <relation>' and eagerly converted EVERY column of EVERY row through duckdb_value_to_protocol, which fails closed on Date32/Timestamp/Time64/Interval/Blob, out-of-i64/u64 HugeInt, and non-finite Float/Double. One such value anywhere in the file killed the binding regardless of what any rule referenced. The lanes diverged because evaluate_batch only materializes when a rule routes to the portable engine, so a pure batch-only set never touched this code at all.

ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED - NOT A 0.5.0 REGRESSION
v0.4.0..v0.5.0 touches only binding_predicates.rs and scalar.rs; run.rs and bindings.rs are untouched, and the Date32 => Err arm predates 0.4.0. Bisected by building both tags against the minimal repro:
  v0.3.1 -> VERIFY PASS exit=0
  v0.4.0 -> failed to materialize binding tape: column FILING_DATE ... exit=2
The break landed in 5531f8e 'feat: integrate binding-qualified predicates', first tagged in v0.4.0. 2e92594 (bd-ch7) is innocent - it only improved the other lane, which is what made the pre-existing break visible by contrast.

0.3.1 WAS NOT CORRECT EITHER
The old converter ended in '_ => Value::String(format!("{value:?}"))'. On v0.3.1 a predicate FILING_DATE == '2026-01-31' reported value "Date32(20484)" / "Date32(20512)" and failed BOTH rows including the matching one. 5531f8e traded silently wrong answers on temporal columns for a loud refusal. Restoring pre-0.4.0 behaviour would be a correctness regression, so the fix does not do that.

FIX - PROJECTION
verify-core/src/validation.rs gains routes_to_portable_engine (now the single classifier both lanes share, so they cannot drift again) and portable_relation_columns, which returns the columns each binding must materialize: declared rule columns, predicate operand columns, and the binding key_fields that localize failures. run.rs projects exactly those, intersected with the columns the relation actually has so E_FIELD_NOT_FOUND still comes from the engine rather than a raw SQL error. A binding no portable rule reads is not materialized. A binding read only for its row count takes a COUNT(*) path that converts no value.

A temporal column a rule DOES reference still refuses - fail-closed preserved, pending bd-286 giving the portable lane a temporal protocol value.

VERIFIED
- reporter's exact case now returns: FAIL SEC_RATE_NONZERO binding=new key.ASSETNUMBER=5-001 field=RATE value=0.0
- 50k x 46-col ABS-EE-shaped tape with 5 unreferenced date columns: PASS in 1.7s
- referenced temporal column: still exit 2, refusal names the column
- gates: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 20/20 test targets green, ubs 0 critical

TESTS
- tests/portable_rules.rs: unreferenced_temporal_columns_do_not_block_materialization, referenced_temporal_columns_still_refuse
- verify-core validation unit tests: portable_columns_cover_only_what_rules_read, batch_only_rules_contribute_no_materialized_columns, row_count_reads_a_relation_without_reading_a_column
- fixtures/inputs/arity1/loans_with_temporal_columns.csv

DOCS
docs/plan.md spine batch executor, AGENTS.md new invariant 5 'Materialization is narrow' (later invariants renumbered), README batch execution context.

title: numbers are rounded through f64: unequal wide integers and decimals compare equal, wrong PASS
description:
WRONG PASS: yes. Affects released 0.6.0, 0.6.1, 0.7.0, 0.7.1 and main 8611980.
Repro (each returns PASS, must FAIL): predicate eq 9007199254740992 over 9007199254740993; sum[9007199254740992,1] eq 9007199254740992; DECIMAL sum[0.1,0.2] gt 0.3; foreign_key child DECIMAL(38,10) 12345678901234567.88 against parent 12345678901234567.89.
unique also reports distinct wide decimals as duplicates (false FAIL).
Test: repro_wide_numbers_compare_exactly
Cause: verify-engine scalar.rs values_equal/compare_values use as_f64; portable_relation.rs sums in f64; verify-duckdb scalar.rs parses DECIMAL into a serde_json Number (f64 without arbitrary_precision). Embedded callers' JSON numbers lose precision when parsed the same way.
Note: both predicate lanes share these scalar functions. Found by bd-5ps (arm S).

Example: v = [9007199254740992, 9007199254740993], max selects ...993 after bd-nx1, but max eq 9007199254740992 still returns PASS until this bead is fixed. bd-nx1 changes no Cargo.toml feature.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
DESIGN (Lane B). No product code changed. Source read at 3848e73. "RUN" = released 0.7.5 (macOS x86_64, checksum verified) unless marked; "CODE" = read, not run.

0. URGENT, NOT ONLY WIDE NUMBERS
verify-built serde_json has neither float_roundtrip nor arbitrary_precision (cargo tree -e features: default, std, indexmap, preserve_order). Its default float parser is not correctly rounded.
RUN: v=985085759598861.9 (CSV), rule literal the identical text: eq FAIL, ne PASS.
RUN: 600 random 16/17-digit values against their own text: eq wrong 81; ne wrong PASS 81; gt wrong PASS 45; lt wrong PASS 36; gte/lte wrong FAIL 36/45. Second sample: 0/400 wrong at 6 and 15 digits, 28/400 at 16, 100/400 at 17, 94/400 at 19 (CSV and JSONL).
RUN: CSV and JSONL loaders gave the correctly rounded value for 600/600 each. The wrong side is the literal in the compiled JSON.
RUN: one rules file: one-step PASS, compile then run FAIL. compile wrote the literal correctly (YAML parsing matched 300/300); run re-reads it with serde_json.
CODE: the same parser converts DuckDB DECIMAL (verify-duckdb scalar.rs; query_rules.rs duckdb_to_json), so DECIMAL data with many digits can be misparsed too (not run).
RUN, scratch crate, serde_json 1.0.149, 100000 each: default differs from the nearest f64 in 0 / 3752 / 26590 / 25976 at 15/16/17/19 digits; float_roundtrip: 0 at all four.

1. WHERE NUMBERS ARE ROUNDED OR LOST
Loading (RUN via typeof() and --explicit; CSV, JSON, JSONL):
- integer within i64: BIGINT, exact.
- integer beyond i64: CSV DOUBLE, rounded. JSON/JSONL: 2^63, 2^63+1 and u64::MAX refuse E_IO (cause not investigated); 2^64+1 and a 30-digit integer load as DOUBLE, rounded.
- any fraction: DOUBLE. 12345678901234567.89 -> 12345678901234568; 1.0000000000000000001 -> 1.0.
- a column mixing 9007199254740993 and 0.5: DOUBLE; the integer arrives as 9007199254740992.0.
- XLSX (CODE): the file stores f64; cmdrvl-tabular writes shortest round-trip text to CSV, which is then type-sniffed. Long digits kept in TEXT cells would be sniffed to numbers and rounded.
- Parquet (CODE): DOUBLE/FLOAT are binary at source. DECIMAL stays exact in DuckDB, then converter does to_string -> serde_json Number -> f64. DECIMAL scale 0 arrives as HugeInt; beyond u64 refuses.
- CRASH (RUN through a query_zero_rows result): CAST to DECIMAL(38,1) of 9999999999999999999999999999.5, and DECIMAL(38,30) 0.5, abort verify (exit 134, no report): rust_decimal panics inside duckdb-rs Decimal::from_i128_with_scale. Binding columns use the same row.get conversion (CODE; no Parquet file was built, so not run).
Rule values:
- compiled JSON: misrounding above; RUN: integer literals 18446744073709551617 and ...999 both eq a DOUBLE 2^64 cell -> PASS (silently rounded).
- YAML: parsed correctly rounded; integers outside i64/u64 are E_BAD_AUTHORING; 12345678901234567.89 compiles to 1.2345678901234568e+16 and 1.0000000000000000001 to 1.0 with no error (RUN).
- tolerance: Option<f64>.
Embedded (CODE): caller supplies serde_json::Value. Without arbitrary_precision it cannot hold a long decimal; a caller parsing with the same build gets the same misrounding.
Comparing and arithmetic (CODE unless RUN):
- scalar.rs values_equal/compare_values: both sides as f64. Predicates eq/ne/in/ordered, portable AND binding lane. RUN: ...993 eq ...992 PASS.
- portable_relation.rs: thresholds (own values_equal/compare_values), tolerance subtraction in f64, sum/avg accumulate in f64. RUN: max ...993 eq ...992 PASS; sum[...992,1] eq ...992 PASS; sum[0.1,0.2] gt 0.3 PASS, eq 0.3 FAIL; sum[100.10,200.20,300.30] eq 600.6 FAIL; avg[0.1,0.2] eq 0.15 FAIL.
- ROW ORDER CHANGES A VERDICT (RUN): rows 1e16,1,-1e16: sum eq 1 FAIL; rows 1e16,-1e16,1: PASS.
- row_count as f64: exact below 2^53.
- min/max selection and unique: exact over received values (bd-nx1, bd-v3r).
- foreign_key: JSON text (bd-v3r). Binding-lane keys: KeyPart f64 plus CAST(.. AS DOUBLE) join and lookup (bd-7k7).
- query_zero_rows: DuckDB compares; verify rounds only its localized output values.
- reports print the received (rounded) value; order.rs and redaction use its text. constraint_hash for run is over file bytes.

2. TWO CONSTRAINTS ON ANY FIX
(a) Exact comparison is NOT automatically safe while loading rounds. A DOUBLE cell rounded from ...993 arrives as ...992.0; today eq literal ...993 PASSes (both round) and ne FAILs. Comparing the received value exactly against integer ...993 makes eq FAIL and ne PASS: a new wrong PASS. Same shape as the foreign_key catch. So loaders come first, or comparisons across integer/fraction forms at |x| >= 2^53 refuse until they do. Small rounded fractions (1.0000000000000000001) are undetectable after loading.
(b) A binary float needs a meaning. Proposed: its value is its shortest round-trip decimal. (Taking the exact binary expansion would make a Parquet DOUBLE 0.1 unequal to literal 0.1.) Then numbers are exact decimals everywhere. docs/plan.md says nothing about precision or summation; this needs a ruling and add-only text.

3. REPRESENTATION OPTIONS (needed only from step 5)
R1 serde_json arbitrary_precision. RUN (scratch crate): keeps long numbers, BUT an f64 field inside an internally tagged enum no longer parses from text ("invalid type: map, expected f64"). Check is internally tagged and holds tolerance, and run parses text, so every artifact with a tolerance would fail to load unless that public field's type changes (it did parse via an intermediate Value). Untagged/flattened f64 also fail. Value equality becomes textual (1.0 != 1.00, 1e2 != 100.0); reports keep 100.2500000000 and write 1e+2; serializing a Value to YAML emits a private wrapper; YAML -> Value still rounds long decimals. Features unify, so twinning (embeds verify-core/engine, pinned rev) and every embedder would get all of it.
R2 a verify-owned scalar in the public API (Relation rows no longer Value): clean, breaking for every embedder.
R3 verify-owned exact number used internally, built from Value (exact for i64/u64; f64 by shortest decimal), plus an ADDITIVE way for loaders and embedded callers to attach exact decimal text to cells Value cannot hold; literals need their source text too. Existing API and bytes stay for values Value already holds. Cost: two carriers, so one conversion function must be the only way into a comparison. Getting literal text from compiled JSON needs either serde_json raw_value (a feature, approval) or a small number-preserving read of our own (design spike).
My recommendation: R3. Not R1.
Dependencies: none required for comparison (sign/digits/exponent compare is small in-house code). Exact sum needs big addition: in-house, or num-bigint (already in Cargo.lock transitively, but a new direct dependency: needs approval). rust_decimal is not an option (96-bit; it is the thing that panics). avg needs no division to decide: compare sum with expected*n, and |sum - expected*n| <= tolerance*n; only the REPORTED avg needs a rounding rule.

4. STEPS, each separately verifiable. Acceptance is not narrowed: the bead closes only after step 8 with no interim refusal left standing.
S1 correctly rounded parsing: enable serde_json float_roundtrip (feature on an existing dependency: Cargo.toml change, NEEDS APPROVAL; no new package expected, Cargo.lock effect not yet checked). Verdicts: only rules whose literal (or DECIMAL value) was misparsed, 16+ digits; both directions, to the correct one; one-step and compiled agree. Report bytes: only where such a number appears. Re-serialized artifacts change in those digits; run hashes do not. No refusals. Embedders in the same build get the fix by unification. I recommend its own P0 bead and a patch release first. Proof: the identical-text property over CSV/JSONL/compiled and one-step, 0 wrong.
S2 no more aborts: DECIMAL that rust_decimal cannot hold, in bindings and query results: read DECIMAL as text in SQL (preferred), else typed refusal as a LABELLED INTERIM. Changes: crash -> verdict or refusal. First build a Parquet repro for the binding path.
S3 exact, order-independent sum/avg over what is received (integers exact; floats by shortest decimal). Verdicts: order-dependent cases, 0.1+0.2 style, wide integer sums. Report bytes: sum observed values (0.30000000000000004 -> 0.3; today sums are written as floats, 19.0; I propose keeping that form wherever f64 holds the result). INTERIM refusal when any input is a float with |x| >= 2^53 (constraint 2a). Needs ruling 2b and the arithmetic choice.
S4 exact comparison of exactly-received values: integer against integer (all i64/u64) in predicates, thresholds, tolerance. ...993 eq ...992 becomes FAIL. Fraction/integer at |x| >= 2^53: INTERIM refusal, labelled, bead open. One shared comparison for scalar.rs and portable_relation.rs. No representation change.
S5 representation (R3) plus rule literals: compiled JSON and YAML keep exact text; literals beyond what can be held stop being rounded silently (interim: refuse at load/compile). Report bytes: values beyond f64 need a ruling (JSON number with all digits, which consumers will themselves round, or a string, which changes the type).
S6 loaders, one at a time, each lifting interim refusals: (a) Parquet DECIMAL/HUGEINT; (b) CSV and XLSX: read columns DuckDB sniffs as DOUBLE as text and parse exactly, keeping today's type decisions; (c) JSON/JSONL: SPIKE FIRST, I have not established that DuckDB can hand over a number's source text; if not, say so and keep the labelled refusal while an alternative is designed (this also covers the E_IO range). Changes: wide values verdict correctly; reports may print more digits.
S7 binding-lane keys (bd-7k7): exact identity and join, no CAST to DOUBLE. S4-S6 do not close it by themselves.
S8 embedded contract and docs: how an embedded caller passes exact decimals; twinning compatibility check; remove interims; then unblock bd-v3r foreign_key (option b can then be revisited, since its 2^53 limit exists only because of rounding).
Ordering: S1, S2 are independent and first. S3 and S4 next. S6 needs S5. S7 after S4/S6a.
Each step: failing tests first; differential arms updated without loosening; released-vs-new comparison of every verdict over a corpus of values loading cannot round (must be identical); report byte comparison on repo fixtures.

5. RULINGS I NEED
Q1 file separate beads? Proposed: literal misparse (P0, S1); DECIMAL abort (P1, S2); row-order-dependent sum (P1, S3); JSON integers in (i64::MAX, u64::MAX] refuse E_IO (P2, observed). I have filed nothing.
Q2 approve serde_json float_roundtrip (S1)?
Q3 binary-float meaning = shortest round-trip decimal?
Q4 representation: R3 (recommended), R2 or R1?
Q5 sum arithmetic: in-house (recommended) or num-bigint?
Q6 interim refusal code: reuse E_BAD_EXPR with a detail reason (recommended; E_SQL_ERROR today for unrepresentable bindings) or a new code?
Q7 report form for numbers f64 cannot hold, and the rounding rule for a reported avg.

NOT ESTABLISHED: Parquet binding behaviour (no file built); XLSX; embedded mode; binding-lane keys in this session (bd-7k7 evidence stands); DuckDB JSON raw number text; cause of the E_IO range; Cargo.lock effect of S1; whether S1 changes performance; twinning's build against any option; releases other than 0.7.5; non-macOS. Random samples measure frequency for those generators only, not real rule files.

title: [CRV1] Amend plan.md: verify consumes canonical relations, provenance via lock/pack
description: Cross-repo initiative canonical-relations-v1. Small docs-only bead. Amend docs/plan.md to state explicitly: (1) verify evaluates already-canonical named relations produced upstream by profile's bounded materialization; it never loads profiles, resolves --profile-id, or rewrites headers. (2) Compiled constraints name canonical fields and are therefore reusable across servicers/formats. (3) Provenance for canonical inputs and the profile bundle is carried by lock (byte hashes, lock.v0 'profiles') and pack membership, not by a receipt field in verify.report.v1. (4) The determinism invariant is unchanged: same compiled constraint bytes plus same binding bytes produce the same ordered report bytes. No code changes. No new report fields.
acceptance_criteria: 1. docs/plan.md states that column alias resolution belongs to upstream profile materialization and rejects runtime verify profile lookup and CLI-only rewriting. 2. The plan specifies the exact canonical-relations-v1 receipt fields verify consumes, validates, reports, or deliberately leaves to pack. 3. Arity-N runs associate provenance per named binding so different raw schemas and profile bundles cannot be conflated. 4. Batch and embedded APIs receive the same structured provenance semantics; embedded execution never needs filesystem profile resolution. 5. Report identity and determinism are restated to cover canonical binding bytes plus any receipt fields that can alter evaluation or replay. 6. Receipt/input/profile mismatch and unsupported-version behavior have explicit refusal ownership and codes if verify validates them. 7. The plan includes a complete profile -> canonicalize -> shape/rvl -> verify -> pack example and records all CRV1 companion bead IDs. 8. Implementation is split into exact-file child beads after the protocol decision; this bead makes no code behavior changes. 9. git diff --check, UBS docs scan, and br dep cycles are clean.
notes: Initiative companions: profile epic bd-3bg; profile contract bd-1ag; profile materializer bd-390; profile conformance bd-2w7; shape integration bd-1y1d; rvl integration bd-3qg. The original generic --profile design was intentionally narrowed after choosing upstream canonicalization. Exact file for this design bead: docs/plan.md only, plus Beads metadata. After approval, split bd-1bh into exact-file implementation lanes if more than one crate or test owner is needed.

title: Lower cross-binding predicates into the portable lane
description:
DEFERRED - real, but not now. bd-3is ships cross-binding predicates in the batch/DuckDB lane first; this lowers them into the portable row-wise executor so the SAME rule runs embedded.

WHY IT MATTERS (docs/plan.md, non-negotiables #3 and #4):
verify is one primitive with two execution contexts - batch validation over locked artifacts on disk, and EMBEDDED validation over materialized candidate state inside twinning and decoding. In the factory context there is no file on disk to hand DuckDB. A batch-only rule cannot gate a decoding convergence step.

The consequence worth caring about: 'origination date is immutable' should be enforceable WHILE decoding is choosing among conflicting claims about a loan, not only after the artifact is sealed. If a convergence step can pick a candidate that silently restates an immutable field, catching it downstream is late.

THE WORK:
crates/verify-engine/src/portable_row.rs evaluates row-wise inside ONE relation. Cross-binding operands need the other binding resolvable per row without a SQL engine: build an index of the counterpart binding keyed by its declared key_fields, then look up per row. Memory profile matters - the indexed side is fully materialized, and CMBS tapes get large.

CONFORMANCE GATE (this is the point of the bead, not an extra):
non-negotiable #3 says a rule marked portable must evaluate with the SAME MEANING in batch and embedded execution. So this needs a differential test: same compiled constraint set + same bindings must produce identical ordered report bytes through the DuckDB lane and the portable lane. Unmatched-key semantics, null handling, and type coercion must agree exactly - they are the three places the two lanes will drift.

Once this lands, the rules bd-3is introduced can be re-marked portable and the batch-only carve-out disappears.

comments.text: bd-ch7 landed in 2e92594cb18377ce5658ce6e5ca1ecce9ae8559d with Option 1 implemented in the DuckDB batch lane only. Portable/embedded still has no temporal protocol Value and no cross-binding lowering; the shared batch/embedded temporal conformance fixture and identical-semantics guarantee remain open here before any temporal cross-binding predicate can be marked portable.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
Scope note from the bd-1ka fix (82f121a, shipped v0.5.1).

Batch materialization now projects only the columns portable rules read, so an
unreferenced temporal column no longer aborts the load. What survives is
narrower and splits cleanly in two:

1. NULLITY over temporal columns - filed separately as bd-5oi. not_null,
   is_null and is_blank need presence, not representation, so this does not
   depend on any of the temporal comparison semantics this bead covers. It
   should land first and independently.

2. VALUE COMPARISON over temporal columns in the portable lane - stays here.
   Still no temporal protocol Value, still no cross-binding lowering, and the
   shared batch/embedded conformance fixture remains the gate.

Also worth recording for whoever picks this up: the pre-0.4.0 converter's
catch-all arm rendered temporals through Rust Debug ("Date32(20484)"), so
portable temporal comparison did not merely refuse before 5531f8e - it answered
wrongly. Any lowering designed here must beat that bar honestly, not restore
it.

routes_to_portable_engine now lives in verify-core/src/validation.rs and is the
single classifier both executors share, so the batch and portable lanes cannot
silently disagree about which rules materialize. That is the drift guard this
bead's conformance requirement assumes.

title: Compile SQL authoring into batch_only query rules

title: Add binding-qualified predicate protocol types and schemas
description:
POST-V0 FOUNDATION for binding-qualified predicates.

## Background
verify currently supports the structured predicate grammar only inside one anchor relation. The approved extension adds an optional binding to every ColumnReference. Omission resolves against Check::Predicate.binding and must preserve all existing artifact bytes and behavior. A distinct binding reference makes the predicate batch_only. Older binaries must fail closed on the new field rather than discard it.

This bead owns the protocol representation and pure constraint analysis needed by later compiler, validator, DuckDB, and CLI lanes. It does not execute rules.

## Protocol contract
- ColumnReference.binding is optional, non-empty when present, and omitted during serialization when absent.
- Expression traversal resolves absent references to the predicate anchor, recursively collects every referenced binding, and derives portability: portable exactly when all references resolve to the anchor; batch_only otherwise.
- Every binding-qualified predicate participant must be declared and have a non-empty key_fields tuple; tuple arity must agree positionally, although physical names may differ.
- New stable refusal codes are E_KEY_INVALID, E_KEY_AMBIGUOUS, and E_KEY_UNMATCHED.
- Existing verify.constraint.v1 and verify.report.v1 artifact families remain the only protocol families.

## Boundaries
Do not add DuckDB code, SQL generation, CLI routing, authoring compilation, scoring, policy, domain vocabulary, or portable cross-binding execution.
design:
## Exact file ownership
- crates/verify-core/src/constraint.rs
- crates/verify-core/src/refusal.rs
- crates/verify-core/src/lib.rs
- crates/verify-core/src/validation.rs (new)
- schemas/verify.constraint.v1.schema.json
- schemas/verify.report.v1.schema.json
- tests/schema_contract.rs
- fixtures/constraints/binding_qualified/maturity_date_immutable.verify.json (new)

## Technical approach
1. Extend ColumnReference with Option<String> binding using skip_serializing_if so legacy serialization is unchanged.
2. Preserve the public Binding.key_fields Vec contract while distinguishing absent from explicitly empty input during deserialization: absent remains the legacy empty/default representation and serializes omitted, while an explicitly present empty array is rejected fail-closed. Do not silently normalize explicit [] into absence.
3. Add pure recursive analysis/validation below the CLI. It must expose resolved binding references, derived portability, and structured validation errors with stable reason values: portability_mismatch, undeclared_reference, missing_key_fields, empty_key_fields, and key_arity_mismatch.
4. Keep row-data defects out of this validator; invalid/duplicate/unmatched runtime keys belong to the DuckDB lane.
5. Add the three refusal variants and next-step guidance to verify-core and the report schema.
6. Update the constraint schema so column_ref admits optional non-empty binding and an explicitly present key_fields array has minItems=1.
7. Add a compiled fixture proving different physical key names can align positionally.

The analysis surface must be deterministic, use ordered collections, and avoid coupling verify-core to files, DuckDB, or CLI error rendering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Existing compiled fixtures deserialize and serialize exactly as before; absent ColumnReference.binding never renders as null.
2. Binding-qualified column references round-trip through Rust types and verify.constraint.v1.schema.json, while unknown fields remain rejected.
3. Recursive analysis finds references inside every predicate form, including all and/or/not branches, in, is_null, and is_blank.
4. Derived portability is portable only when every reference resolves to the anchor and batch_only when any reference resolves elsewhere.
5. Pure validation rejects undeclared references, declared/derived portability mismatch, missing or empty participant key_fields, and positional key arity mismatch with stable reason/detail data.
6. E_KEY_INVALID, E_KEY_AMBIGUOUS, and E_KEY_UNMATCHED serialize through verify.report.v1 and provide actionable next steps.
7. key_fields remains optional for rules that do not require it, but an explicitly present array cannot be empty.
8. Unit and schema-contract tests cover valid legacy, valid binding-qualified, and every structural rejection boundary.
9. No execution, authoring, CLI, or embedded behavior is added in this bead.

- schema_contract coverage for the new compiled fixture, optional binding, minItems=1, and refusal-code enum.
- Run cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, and ubs --diff.

title: Add ALIGNMENT_UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE_RATE constraint to catch extra-row inflation
description:
## Problem

Plain benchmark scores matched rows only. An extractor that emits garbage extra rows
can still achieve F1=1 on the matched subset because UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE rows are
filtered out before benchmark sees them. The alignment contract
(CANDIDATE_ALIGNMENT_CONTRACT.md#L142) explicitly flags this gap.

The existing verify constraint set (tournament.bdc_soi.phase1.v0.constraint.json)
checks for ambiguous rows, duplicate matches, and enum validity — but does not check
the RATE of unmatched candidate rows relative to total alignment rows.

## Proposed fix

Add a new batch_only constraint rule ALIGNMENT_UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE_RATE to the verify
constraint JSON. Use the existing query_zero_rows pattern: a SQL query that returns
zero rows when the rate is acceptable, one row when it exceeds the threshold.

Draft rule shape:

    {
      "id": "ALIGNMENT_UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE_RATE",
      "severity": "error",
      "portability": "batch_only",
      "check": {
        "op": "query_zero_rows",
        "bindings": ["alignment"],
        "query": "SELECT 'alignment' AS binding, 'unmatched_candidate_rate' AS field, ROUND(CAST(uc AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(total, 0), 4) AS value FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE match_status = 'UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE') AS uc, COUNT(*) AS total FROM alignment) WHERE CAST(uc AS FLOAT) / NULLIF(total, 0) > 0.10"
      }
    }

The 0.10 threshold (10% unmatched candidates) is a starting point — may need
calibration against live tournament runs. The constraint file lives in
cmdrvl-context/docs/09-plans/tournament/verify/ but the verify tool itself
needs to support this query pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ALIGNMENT_UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE_RATE rule added to tournament.bdc_soi.phase1.v0.constraint.json
- [ ] verify tool passes the rule on current baseline runs (which have 0% unmatched candidates)
- [ ] verify tool fails the rule on a synthetic fixture with >10% unmatched candidate rows
- [ ] Threshold is documented in the constraint JSON or charter template

## Context

Feedback finding 3: "The ranking story can promote flattering scores instead of honest
extractors." This is Pass 2 item 1 from the tournament doc review (2026-03-14).
close_reason: Added ALIGNMENT_UNMATCHED_CANDIDATE_RATE to the tournament constraint, documented the 0.10 threshold, verified baseline alignments still PASS, and proved a synthetic >10% unmatched-candidate alignment fails only this rule.

title: Epic: batch-only binding-qualified predicates over keyed relations
description:
POST-v0 PROTOCOL EXTENSION. This is aligned with verify because it adds a domain-neutral, declared arity-N constraint over named relations; CMBS vocabulary remains in versioned constraint data. It is not aligned as an unplanned code-only change: docs/plan.md currently declares predicate portable and query_zero_rows the only batch-only rule kind. Amend the plan and protocol contract before implementation.

First increment only: add optional binding to ColumnReference. An absent binding resolves against Check::Predicate.binding and preserves every existing artifact. A reference to a different binding makes that predicate explicitly batch_only. The structured predicate AST is lowered deterministically for DuckDB execution over relations already loaded in one BatchContext; operators do not author SQL. Embedded execution refuses the rule with E_BATCH_ONLY_RULE until bd-286 supplies portable lowering.

The protocol amendment must pin the row domain and join contract. Evaluation is anchored on Check::Predicate.binding. Every referenced binding must be declared and expose a non-empty key_fields tuple with compatible arity; components match positionally so physical key names may differ. Participating key tuples must be unique. A missing counterpart, duplicate/ambiguous key, missing field, or incomparable operand is a typed refusal, never an implicit PASS/FAIL or DuckDB coercion. Rows present only in a non-anchor binding are outside this rule invocation. Null behavior and scalar comparison semantics must be explicit and shared with the portable evaluator.

No new domain ops, scoring, policy decisions, or raw SQL enter the artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
1. docs/plan.md is amended before code to admit batch_only predicate rules with binding-qualified operands, including compatibility, key alignment, null/type, refusal, localization, and determinism semantics.
2. The constraint schema and Rust types accept optional ColumnReference.binding; omission preserves existing bytes/meaning. Compiler and validator collect every referenced binding, emit batch_only for a distinct binding reference, and reject a contradictory portable declaration.
3. Batch evaluation uses the existing DuckDB connection and structured AST, covers the full declared predicate grammar, and does not expose generated SQL as authoring or a second protocol.
4. Missing/undeclared bindings, absent or incompatible key_fields, duplicate key tuples, unmatched anchor keys, missing fields, and incomparable operand types produce stable typed refusal envelopes with actionable detail.
5. Each failed anchor row produces one deterministically ordered affected entry localized to the anchor binding/key and to a field/value when the expression permits unambiguous localization.
6. Embedded execution refuses these rules with E_BATCH_ONLY_RULE. Existing single-binding portable predicates remain byte- and behavior-compatible.
7. Schema, compile, validate, refusal, CLI end-to-end, and determinism fixtures cover PASS, FAIL, and every new refusal boundary.
notes:
Treat this as an epic, not a one-agent file grab. After the protocol semantics are approved, split exact-file child beads for: (a) docs/schema/core types, (b) portable authoring and validation, (c) DuckDB AST lowering/execution, and (d) CLI integration plus conformance fixtures. bd-nug and the predicate comparability bug must land first. Portable/factory lowering remains bd-286.

Execution graph created after protocol approval:
- bd-3a3: protocol types, pure validation, schemas, refusal codes, and schema fixtures.
- bd-1aw: structured JSON/YAML authoring plus compiled-artifact validation; blocked by bd-3a3.

- bd-5oj: CLI routing, end-to-end conformance, docs, and final gates; blocked by bd-1aw and bd-1e2.
Close this epic only after all four children close. bd-286 remains the separate deferred portable/factory lane.

comments.author: Zac Ruiz
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION after hands-on testing against real SEC ABS-EE tapes (2026-09-01). Four findings; the bead as written covers only the first.

1. NOT 'unsupported' - SILENTLY WRONG. An operand authored as {binding: old, column: MATURITYDATE} compiles to {column: MATURITYDATE}: serde drops the unknown 'binding' key without error. Both operands collapse to the same column in the same binding, so the rule becomes X == X, always true.
     authored: {'binding': 'old', 'column': 'MATURITYDATE'}
     compiled: {'column': 'MATURITYDATE'}
     result:   VERIFY PASS, passed_rules: 1, severity_band: CLEAN
   An author writes an immutability rule, sees CLEAN, concludes maturity dates never changed. Same class as the MCP unknown-args problem.

2. SPLIT OUT AS IMMEDIATE P1 BUG: #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on ColumnReference. Independent of the feature; converts today's silent tautology into a compile error. Should land BEFORE the feature.

3. JOIN OWNER (was underspecified): verify-engine materializes the joined relation before portable_row.rs evaluates, keyed on each binding's declared key_fields. Open: (a) must bindings declare compatible key_fields (both ASSETNUMBER here, but a loan-tape/property-tape join would not), (b) what an unmatched key yields. Recommend a typed refusal.

4. RELATED SILENT FAILURE, same family: literals are type-strict and mismatches evaluate false forever rather than refusing.
     eq: [{column: v}, "0"]  -> PASS, never fires (string literal vs numeric cell)
     eq: [{column: v}, 0]    -> FAIL, correct
   'Operands not comparable' should be a REFUSAL, not a negative - same argument as shape refusing an incomparable pair.

comments.author: Zac Ruiz
comments.text:
DUCKDB LANE — a much smaller first increment exists (verified 2026-09-01).

verify already embeds DuckDB 1.4.4 via the verify-duckdb crate. crates/verify-duckdb/src/bindings.rs loads EVERY --bind into a DuckDB temp table in one session:
  CREATE TEMP TABLE {relation} AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto('{path}', nullstr='...');
  (also read_json_auto / read_ndjson_auto / read_parquet)

So when 'verify run --bind old=a.csv --bind new=b.csv' runs, both filings are ALREADY co-resident as relations. query_rules.rs (op query_zero_rows) already executes arbitrary SQL across them, which proves the plumbing.

CONSEQUENCE: cross-binding predicates in the batch/DuckDB lane are close to free - the join key is already declared in each binding's key_fields, and it is a SELECT. That is far smaller than the verify-engine work this bead currently describes, which is the PORTABLE lane (crates/verify-engine/src/portable_row.rs, row-wise, no SQL engine).

The compiled artifact already carries per-rule 'portability' (observed: "portability": "portable"), so a batch-only rule family is already modelled.

PROPOSED SPLIT: ship cross-binding predicates as batch-only first, marked non-portable; lower them into the portable row-wise lane as a second increment.

WHY THE PORTABLE LANE EXISTS (docs/plan.md, not incidental):
verify is ONE primitive with TWO execution contexts -
  - Spine / CLI context: batch validation over locked artifacts on disk
  - Factory / runtime context: EMBEDDED validation over materialized candidate state inside twinning and decoding
A portable rule must evaluate with the same MEANING in both. Non-negotiable #3: 'Portable rules are truly portable.' Non-negotiable #4: 'Batch-only rules stay explicit. Embedded execution must refuse them rather than silently ignoring or approximating them.'

So the portable lane is not a lightweight fallback - it is what lets the same constraint set validate candidate state INSIDE twinning/decoding, where there is no file on disk to hand DuckDB. An immutability rule that only runs batch cannot gate a decoding convergence step.

THE REAL DECISION for this bead: are cross-binding immutability rules needed inside the factory runtime (decoding/twinning), or only over sealed artifacts on disk? If the former, the portable lane is mandatory and the DuckDB shortcut is only a staging step. If the latter, batch-only may be the permanent home. That decision is not made here.

title: Nullity-only rules over temporal columns should not need a temporal protocol value
description:
The nullity tier (not_null, is_null, is_blank) asks only whether a value is
present. It needs no representation of the value itself. But batch
materialization still converts every projected column into a protocol scalar,
so a nullity-only rule over a DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIME/INTERVAL column aborts the
load:

  failed to materialize binding tape: column origination_date:
  DuckDB date value cannot be represented as a protocol scalar

CONFIRMED on 0.5.1 for ALL THREE nullity ops, not just not_null:
  not_null columns: [origination_date]        -> materialization error
  predicate not(is_null {origination_date})   -> materialization error
  predicate not(is_blank {origination_date})  -> materialization error

Caution when reproducing: a blank cell anywhere in the column defeats DuckDB's
DATE inference and the column loads as VARCHAR, which passes and hides the bug.
Use a fully populated temporal column (fixtures/inputs/arity1/
loans_with_temporal_columns.csv).

RELATION TO bd-1ka (closed, 82f121a): bd-1ka was that an UNREFERENCED column
aborted the load. That is fixed - materialization now projects only what
portable rules read. This bead is the narrower survivor: a column a nullity
rule DOES reference, where the reference needs no value.

WHY NOT JUST A PLACEHOLDER: substituting a sentinel for present temporals gives
correct nullity verdicts but lies in reports. portable_row.rs
extract_localization returns the row value for IsNull/IsBlank affected entries,
so a rule asserting `is_null: {column: maturity_date}` that FAILS (value
present) would render the sentinel as the field value. Nullity must stay honest
about localization.

LIKELY SHAPE: verify-engine's Relation needs to distinguish "absent/null" from
"present but not representable as a protocol scalar", so the nullity tier reads
presence while any op needing the value refuses explicitly instead of aborting
the load. That touches the embedded lane and the report contract, so it wants a
plan amendment rather than a point patch in run.rs.

SCOPE BOUNDARY vs bd-286: this does NOT require portable temporal comparison
semantics or cross-binding lowering. It only requires presence to be knowable
without representation. It is worth doing independently and first, because
not_null on MATURITYDATE / ORIGINATIONDATE / REPORTINGPERIODENDDATE is a
foundational credit-surveillance rule shape over SEC ABS-EE tapes, and today
none of it runs.

Value comparison on temporal columns in the portable lane remains bd-286.

title: Integrate binding-qualified predicates through CLI and conformance gates
description:
CLI INTEGRATION AND CONFORMANCE gate for binding-qualified batch predicates.

## Background
The protocol, structured compiler, validator, and DuckDB executor land in separate lanes. This bead connects them through the reference verify run path and proves the complete operator contract. It is the final child of bd-3is and must leave existing portable single-binding predicates byte- and behavior-compatible.

Batch execution routes anchor-only predicates through verify-engine and binding-qualified predicates through verify-duckdb. Embedded execution must refuse the latter with E_BATCH_ONLY_RULE; it must never approximate, ignore, or reinterpret them.

## Outcome contract
- PASS/FAIL/REFUSAL and exit codes remain 0/1/2.
- JSON emits one verify.report.v1 object on stdout.
- Failures localize to the anchor binding/key with optional field/value only when unambiguous.
- Runtime structural defects map to stable typed refusal envelopes.
- Identical compiled/input bytes yield byte-identical reports.
- Row-order permutations preserve semantic results/refusal choice after intentionally different input hashes are excluded.

## Boundaries
Do not implement portable cross-binding lowering; that remains deferred in bd-286. Do not add scoring, policy decisions, winner selection, domain-specific operators, raw SQL authoring, caches, or config.

- crates/verify-cli/src/run.rs

1. Run shared compiled-contract validation before binding/rule evaluation and map invalid compiled artifacts to E_BAD_CONSTRAINTS.
2. Partition predicate rules by derived/validated portability. Preserve current verify-engine execution for portable predicates; call the new DuckDB executor only for binding-qualified batch_only predicates.
3. Replace CLI-local DuckDB Value conversion with the shared verify-duckdb conversion so batch paths cannot drift.
4. Map every DuckDB predicate error into a VerifyReport refusal with the pinned code, message, detail, next_step, execution_mode=batch, constraint identity, and available binding identities. Never emit a partial RuleResult on refusal.
5. Preserve normal summary calculation and canonical report sorting.
6. Prove embedded execution rejects the same compiled cross-binding rule with E_BATCH_ONLY_RULE while anchor-only predicates retain batch/embedded parity.
7. Register dedicated integration suites and use the compiled fixture from the foundation plus the authoring fixture from the compiler lane.
8. Update README operator examples and AGENTS rule-tier/file-map guidance only after behavior and gates pass. Keep the post-v0 batch-only status and bd-286 boundary explicit.

Non-scalar and unrepresentable E_KEY_INVALID variants remain mandatory DuckDB unit cases because supported loaders may reject nested values earlier.
5. A failed anchor row produces exactly one affected entry with complete anchor key. Multi-column comparisons omit ambiguous field/value; one-anchor-column versus literal retains them.

comments.text:
DESIGN (Lane B, posted before test code). Head 8611980. Tests only.

## What each lane really evaluates
`routes_to_portable_engine` (validation.rs:290) is false only for query_zero_rows and batch_only predicates. In batch, `evaluate_batch` (run.rs) sends unique, not_null, portable predicate, row_count, aggregate_compare and foreign_key to **verify-engine**, over rows DuckDB loaded. So "the same portable artifact in `verify run` and embedded" compares ONE evaluator with itself; it can only find ingestion/materialization differences. verify-duckdb decides rule truth itself only in (a) binding_predicates.rs and (b) query_rules.rs.

What existing tests prove: tests/embedding_equivalence.rs compares EmbeddedExecutor with a helper that calls the same portable_row/portable_relation functions on the same in-memory Relation; it never opens DuckDB (it proves report assembly and the batch-only refusals). tests/portable_rules.rs runs the CLI against hand-written expectations; no second lane.

## Three arms, each labelled for what it can and cannot prove
**P: predicate, same AST, two evaluators.** Portable artifact: binding `a`, unqualified refs, run by EmbeddedExecutor on JSON rows built by the generator. DuckDB artifact: bindings `a` and `twin` (same key_fields, both bound to one typed Parquet file of the same rows), with a seeded non-empty subset of column refs rewritten to `{binding: twin}`, run by `verify_duckdb::evaluate_binding_predicate`. With unique non-null keys the join pairs each row with its copy, so the truth value must be identical.
Forcing proof, asserted per case: routes_to_portable_engine is true for the first and false for the second; EmbeddedExecutor refuses the second with E_BATCH_ONLY_RULE; portable_row::evaluate_rule rejects it as unsupported.
Compared: verdict vs refusal, refusal code, status, violation_count, set of failing row keys. NOT compared: affected field/value, because the rewrite moves a column off the anchor and the two lanes' localization then differs by construction.
Shared code (blind spot): verify_engine::scalar (values_equal, compare_values, is_blank). A scalar bug is invisible to P; arm S is what covers it. AST walk, join, value conversion, preflight and report assembly are separate.
Excluded: duplicate, null or temporal keys (the binding-qualified contract requires a unique non-null protocol-scalar key, portable predicates do not). Those are asserted separately as the documented refusals.

**S: the five other kinds, plus predicates, against DuckDB's own semantics.** unique, not_null, foreign_key, row_count and aggregate_compare have NO verify-duckdb implementation. The only way DuckDB can decide them is `query_zero_rows`, so this arm is verify-engine vs a test-authored SQL transcription of the plan text, run by `execute_query_rules` on the same Parquet. It is NOT "the same rule artifact"; it is two implementations of one documented rule. Every mismatch is triaged against docs/plan.md, and a mistake in my SQL is a test bug, not a product bug. SQL queries have query_zero_rows routing asserted.
Compared: pass/fail and the multiset of failing keys (row-level kinds); pass/fail only for row_count and aggregate_compare. Not compared: refusals, report values.
Excluded: shapes the plan does not define (avg/min/max over zero rows or over nulls where the plan is silent are listed as observed, not asserted). The blank rule uses an explicit Unicode White_Space class, not DuckDB trim().

**I: ingestion, the plan's "portable means the same in batch and embedded" (plan l.105, l.148).** Same compiled artifact: EmbeddedExecutor on the generator's JSON rows vs the `verify run` binary (CARGO_BIN_EXE_verify, --explicit --json) on typed Parquet and JSONL of the same rows; targeted CSV only where intent is unambiguous (null vs empty string, quoted strings). The evaluator is the same on both sides, and the arm says so. Compared: the full results array (including affected key/field/value) and outcome; refusal code.

**T: temporal.** The portable protocol has no temporal scalar, so no temporal VALUE rule can be evaluated by both. In DuckDB, same-family column-to-column comparisons are native. Oracle (not the same rule): DuckDB native over DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP vs the portable engine over canonical fixed-width ISO strings, where byte order equals time order. Nullity (is_null, is_blank, not_null) over temporal columns is probed in all lanes.

## Generator
Hand-rolled SplitMix64, no new dependency; every assertion message carries arm and case seed. Value pools: null vs "" vs ASCII and Unicode whitespace, zero-width space; composed vs decomposed unicode, case variants, non-BMP; BIGINT around 2^53 and at i64 limits, UBIGINT, HUGEINT; DECIMAL(18,2)/(38,10); DOUBLE with -0.0, subnormals, f64::MAX; NaN/Inf both as DOUBLE values (Parquet; JSON cannot carry them, so no embedded side) and as strings; BOOLEAN; DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP; zero rows; all-null columns; duplicate rows/keys; cross-type literals; tolerance exactly at, just under and just over |observed - expected|.

## When lanes disagree
No product change, no generator narrowing, no red test on main. Each defect gets a bead, a minimized repro committed as `#[ignore = "<bead>"]` asserting the DOCUMENTED behaviour, and a known-divergence entry in the generated run that matches only that exact shape AND both exact outcomes. Anything else fails; an entry that no case hits also fails, so a fix forces its removal. This pins current wrong behaviour in the classifier, visibly and by bead id; tell me if you prefer another way to keep main green.

## Planted disagreement
git-archive export with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, Edit tool only: break the DuckDB-lane AST walk (arm P must fail) and a portable relation rule (arm S must fail).

## Files
crates/verify-cli/tests/lane_differential.rs (auto-discovered, so no Cargo.toml change; verify-cli already depends on all three crates, duckdb and serde_json). No Cargo.lock change.

title: Cross-binding predicates refuse all temporal operands (date/timestamp/time/interval)
description:
VERIFIED on verify 0.4.0 against real SEC ABS-EE tapes (2026-09-02), after bd-3is shipped.

Cross-binding predicates work for numbers and strings but refuse on every temporal type:
  ORIGINALLOANAMOUNT (number) -> VERIFY PASS, and FAILs correctly when a cell is mutated
  ORIGINATORNAME     (string) -> VERIFY PASS
  MATURITYDATE       (date)   -> REFUSAL E_BAD_EXPR
     detail: {reason: unrepresentable_operand, value_type: date,
              field: MATURITYDATE, key: {ASSETNUMBER: 1}}

ROOT CAUSE (crates/verify-duckdb/src/scalar.rs:40 duckdb_value_to_protocol):
  representable:   Null Boolean TinyInt SmallInt Int BigInt HugeInt UTinyInt
                   USmallInt UInt UBigInt Float Double Decimal Text Enum
  unrepresentable: Timestamp, Date32, Time64, Interval, Blob
The whole temporal family is excluded. The adjacent test is named
'converts_every_protocol_scalar_family_without_coercion', so this is deliberate:
the protocol Value has no temporal type, and rendering a date means choosing a
string format, which is a coercion. Refusing is defensible - but it blocks the
motivating use case.

WHY THIS MATTERS: temporal columns are the MOST important immutable fields in a
loan tape. MATURITYDATE, ORIGINATIONDATE, FIRSTLOANPAYMENTDUEDATE,
POSTMODIFICATIONMATURITYDATE. 'Origination date is immutable' - the exact rule
bd-3is was filed to enable - cannot be expressed today. The entire MONOTONIC
tier is temporal too (paid-through date must never move backwards), so it is
blocked as well.

THREE OPTIONS, in ascending cost:

1. EVALUATE WITHOUT REPRESENTING. For a cross-binding comparison the value never
   needs to become a protocol Value - only the VERDICT does. eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte
   between two binding-qualified operands can be evaluated in SQL inside DuckDB,
   which compares temporals natively and exactly. Representation is only needed
   when a value appears in a failure report, where it can be rendered via an
   explicit DuckDB cast. This preserves 'no implicit coercion' because no
   coercion enters the comparison at all. Recommended.

2. EXPLICIT OPT-IN CAST in the constraint set, e.g. an operand-level cast to a
   declared canonical form (ISO-8601). Coercion becomes authored and visible
   rather than implicit. More authoring burden, but honest.

3. ADD A TEMPORAL TYPE to the protocol Value model with a declared canonical
   representation. Largest blast radius: touches the wire contract, the portable
   lane, and every consumer of a verify report.

Option 1 is the smallest change that unblocks the real rules and keeps the
no-coercion property the current design is protecting.

NOTE FOR THE PORTABLE LANE (bd-286): whichever option is chosen must hold in
BOTH lanes with the same meaning. Option 1 is DuckDB-native, so bd-286 will need
an equivalent temporal comparison in the row-wise executor - and that is exactly
the kind of place the two lanes drift. Worth deciding here, not there.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR REVIEW (2026-09-02, Claude): root cause CONFIRMED in source. crates/verify-duckdb/src/scalar.rs duckdb_value_to_protocol maps Timestamp, Date32, Time64, Interval and Blob to unrepresentable(), distinct from the non_scalar() class used for list/struct/array/map/union. Two failure classes, as described.

REFINEMENT TO OPTION 1 — the bead treats the temporal path as one thing, but there are TWO call paths with different costs:

(a) PROJECTION values (binding_predicates.rs:957) push `Result<Value, DuckValueError>` — the error is DEFERRED and only surfaces when a predicate actually touches that column. This is the path Option 1 targets, and here Option 1 is genuinely cheap: move eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte into the SQL, and only render on the failure path.

(b) KEY components (binding_predicates.rs:582 and :924) must become protocol Values for tuple identity, joining and dedupe. Option 1 does NOT free this path. A temporal used as a KEY field still needs representation.

LANDMINE IN OPTION 1 BLAST RADIUS — duckdb_value_sort_key (scalar.rs:124) enumerates null/bool/number/string and then falls through to `other => format!("99:{other:?}")`, i.e. Rust Debug formatting. That sort_key is joined at binding_predicates.rs:637 and orders KeyIssue records, which IS the ordered report byte stream the determinism invariant protects ("same compiled constraint bytes plus same binding bytes produce the same ordered report bytes", restated in docs/plan.md by bd-21h).

Today this is unreachable for temporals because they refuse first. The moment temporal operands become permissible, that fallback becomes live and report ordering would depend on the Debug representation of a third-party DuckDB type: not chronological, and not stable across a duckdb crate bump. Any option chosen here must give temporals an explicit, ordered, contract-stable sort key rather than inheriting the `99:{other:?}` fallback. That is a determinism bug waiting to be introduced, and it is invisible in the number/string testing that passes today.

CONCUR with Option 1 as the recommendation, with the two amendments above: it is the only option that keeps the no-coercion property intact, since no coercion enters the comparison at all.

NOTE ON bd-286 (portable lane): agreed this must be decided here, not there. Option 1 is DuckDB-native, so the row-wise executor needs an equivalent temporal comparison with IDENTICAL semantics and IDENTICAL ordering. Recommend a shared conformance fixture exercising the same temporal predicates through both lanes and asserting byte-identical reports, so the drift is caught by a test rather than by a customer.

title: Replace unsalted sha256 redaction tokens: deterministic ordinal refs by default, opt-in keyed HMAC (VERIFY_REDACTION_KEY)
description:
## Background
bd-q4d (closed) made `verify run` redact failing-row keys and cell values by default. The token is `redacted:sha256:<16 hex>` = the first 8 bytes of an UNSALTED SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the value (`crates/verify-cli/src/redact.rs` `token`). The module header and robot-docs say so honestly: a low-entropy value (a status code, a small integer, a short name) is recoverable by dictionary guess. Operator decision (2026-11-25, the same decision made for decoding bd-1pv): remove the hash from the default output and replace it with deterministic ordinal references; offer an opt-in operator-held key for stable cross-run markers. A random per-run salt is REJECTED because it makes default output non-reproducible, and reproducible output is a core property of this tool family.

## Required behavior
1. DEFAULT (no key): NO hash of any key or cell value appears anywhere in the report. Each distinct value in the EMITTED entries gets an ordinal reference in order of first appearance while walking the report in its output order: keys get `redacted:ref:k1`, `redacted:ref:k2`, ...; cell values get `redacted:ref:v1`, `redacted:ref:v2`, ... (two separate namespaces, so a key and a cell holding equal bytes do NOT share a ref and leak that equality). Equality is decided on the canonical JSON of the value. The numbering is computed over the entries actually emitted (so `--sample-affected N` cannot leak anything about unsampled rows), and the result is byte-identical on re-running the same input with the same flags. Document plainly what refs reveal (the equality pattern within the output and the number of distinct values, not their content) and that refs are not comparable across runs on different inputs or different sampling.
2. KEYED (operator supplies a key): HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical JSON of the value with the operator key, rendered `redacted:hmac-sha256:<32 hex>` (128 bits). Stable across runs and inputs for the key holder, unguessable without the key. Key source: environment variable `VERIFY_REDACTION_KEY` (declare it in operator.json env_vars; document in README and robot-docs). The key must be at least 16 bytes: an empty or too-short key is a typed REFUSAL (exit 2, a new E_ code declared in operator.json and refusals[] and covered by the contract's refusal-source check), never a silent fallback to ordinals. The key value must never appear in any output, error message, witness record or doctor report; doctor may report only whether a key is configured.
3. The old `redacted:sha256:<16 hex>` tokens are REMOVED. Find downstream consumers of that exact string (in-repo docs, fixtures, tests, other repos, receipts or catalog skills that parse verify output) and list them in the bead comment with the migration. SQL error text stays withheld by default; `--explicit` is unchanged (raw values and error text).
4. Keep what bd-q4d established: column, binding and rule names, rule SQL text, file paths and counts are not redacted (document it again); the JSON shape is unchanged (strings stay strings, so existing consumers that only check for presence keep working).
5. No random-number dependency (no salt). The keyed mode needs only HMAC: use the `hmac` crate with the existing `sha2`; no unsafe, no hand-rolled crypto. Say which crate and version you added.

## Tests (real, with planted negatives)
- Default: two runs byte-identical; equal values share a ref within a namespace and distinct values never do; numbering follows first appearance; a key and a cell with equal bytes get refs in different namespaces; `--sample-affected 1` numbers only emitted entries.
- Dictionary negative: compute the OLD token for a known planted canary (first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of its canonical JSON, 16 hex) and assert it does NOT appear in default or keyed output; assert no 16- or 64-hex string derived from a value appears in default output at all.
- Keyed: a fixed test key gives a fixed expected marker (known-answer test, cross-checked with an independent implementation such as `openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac` pasted in the comment); same key => identical markers across runs and inputs; different key => different markers.
- Key hygiene: a planted key string never appears in stdout, stderr, the report, a witness record or doctor output; empty and 15-byte keys are refused with the typed code; a 16-byte key is accepted.
- The bd-q4d canary tests still pass in every channel (zero raw keys and cells in stdout and stderr, JSON and human, with and without `--sample-affected`); `--explicit` restores raw values.
- golden_rules and the contract checks pass at the current spine-rules pin; run the repo's whole `--lib` suite AND every test file that mentions describe, operator, capabilities or redaction.

## Process
DuckDB is compiled in this repo: one cargo command at a time, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 and CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3, no `cargo clean`, do not switch CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Real code, real tests, hand-written edits (no rewrite scripts).

## Out of scope
Anything other than the redaction token format and the new key handling.

title: Align verify doctor unhealthy exit code (2 -> 1), capabilities schema, and empty witness query exit code (1 -> 0)
description:
## Background & Evidence

1. **Doctor unhealthy exit code:** `crates/verify-cli/src/doctor.rs:106` returns exit `2` when a health check fails (`if self.ok() { 0 } else { 2 }`), whereas sibling tools (`shape`, `canon`) return exit `1` for findings and reserve `2` for CLI/usage errors.
