title: Add pure-Rust document quote, byte-span, and numeric-scale grounding check in verify-engine
description:
## Context
When an LLM or extraction pipeline reads unstructured/semi-structured filings or contracts (e.g., SEC 8-K/10-K HTML, Exhibit 99.1, PDF text, credit amendments) and emits structured claims with citations, the classic deterministic double-check is proving that every claimed quote and number actually appears in the pinned source bytes.

Putting this check inside pure-Rust, `wasm32`-clean `verify-engine` (zero DuckDB required) keeps the contract unified: it verifies against `--lock` (`lock.v0`), emits standard `verify.report.v1` (redacted by default unless `--explicit`), feeds `assess` and `pack` directly, and runs identically in CLI and browser WASM.

## Scope
Add a document-grounding check mode (e.g., `verify ground <CLAIMS_JSONL> --bind <NAME=DOC> [--lock <LOCK>]` or a `grounding` constraint family in `verify-core`/`verify-engine`):
1. **Source pin:** Verify each referenced source document against `--lock` (`lock.v0` `blake3:` / `sha256:`).
2. **Verbatim quote & byte-span check:** Verify claimed `quote` matches the exact bytes at `byte_span` (or locate exact canonical byte offsets in raw bytes / HTML-stripped canonical text if `byte_span` is omitted), emitting deterministic failures (`E_QUOTE_NOT_FOUND`, `E_SPAN_MISMATCH`) on fabrication or drift.
3. **Numeric value + scale grounding:** When a claim asserts a numeric `value` (and optional `unit` / `scale`, e.g., `42_500_000` from `$42.5 million` or `42,500` in thousands), verify a compatible numeric surface form exists inside the cited span (catching off-by-1000x scale hallucinations and wrong-column extractions: `E_NUMBER_NOT_IN_SPAN`, `E_SCALE_MISMATCH`).
4. **Zero-retention default output:** Emit `PASS`/`FAIL`, rule/claim ID, canonical byte offsets, and ordinal/keyed redaction refs by default; emit raw quoted excerpts only under `--explicit`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure-Rust grounding engine lives in `verify-engine` (no DuckDB dependency, compiles cleanly under `wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
- Verifies exact byte spans, whitespace/HTML-normalized quotes, and numeric value + scale representations (e.g., millions/thousands/percent/bps) against `--lock`-pinned documents.
- Emits standard `verify.report.v1` compatible with `assess` and `pack`, with zero raw quote/value leakage unless `--explicit` is passed.
- Regression tests cover valid 8-K HTML quote + numeric scale match, fabricated quote, wrong byte span, and 1000x scale mismatch.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
Design before coding — first slice

CLI shape: add a verify ground <CLAIMS_JSONL> --bind <NAME=DOCUMENT>... --lock <LOCKFILE>... [--json] [--explicit] subcommand. Each --bind names one source document; each claim selects its document with source. Grounding is a distinct command family, not a new verify.constraint.v1 rule kind, so the existing constraint protocol and execution paths stay unchanged.

Claims input: JSONL, one object per line:
{"claim_id":"C1","source":"filing","quote":"Revenue was $42.5 million.","byte_span":{"start":123,"end":148},"value":42.5,"unit":"USD","scale":"millions"}
claim_id, source, quote, and byte_span.start/end are required for this first slice; value, unit, and scale are optional as a group for numeric checks. byte_span is a half-open UTF-8 byte range into the raw bound document. scale is exactly one of units, thousands, millions, percent, or bps; value is the printed mantissa, so 42.5 + millions means 42,500,000 base units, while 4.25 + percent means 0.0425 and 125 + bps means 0.0125. Numeric matching will parse signed decimal surfaces with optional commas, currency/percent markers, and scale words/abbreviations, then compare exact decimal rationals after applying those scale factors. No floating-point tolerance or currency conversion.

Quote normalization: first compare quote UTF-8 bytes exactly to document[start..end]. If exact bytes differ, compare both sides after Unicode whitespace normalization: trim leading/trailing whitespace and collapse every Unicode whitespace run to one ASCII space. This is a pass with normalized-match semantics when equal. HTML tags/entities and document-wide quote search are deferred until the first four checks are solid; no HTML normalization is claimed by this slice.

Lock pinning: every bound document is checked against every provided lock.v0 member selected by exact normalized path or one unique basename, using the member bytes_hash prefix rule (sha256: or blake3:). verify-engine has no reusable shared lock helper dependency; the existing helper lives in verify-duckdb, so the pure-Rust implementation will use the same algorithm-by-prefix semantics in a new engine module. If Cargo.toml dependencies are needed, I will name each crate and purpose before pushing.

Report mapping: reuse verify_core::report::VerifyReport, BindingReport, RuleResult, and AffectedEntry; do not fork verify.report.v1. The report uses constraint_set_id=grounding.v1, the claims JSONL SHA-256 as constraint_hash, one existing relation-shaped binding entry per document with content hash and lock verification, and deterministic claim/check rule IDs. Quote and numeric failures are domain FAIL results whose IDs carry E_QUOTE_NOT_FOUND, E_SPAN_MISMATCH, E_NUMBER_NOT_IN_SPAN, or E_SCALE_MISMATCH; malformed claims, missing bindings, bad spans, unreadable documents, and bad locks are REFUSALs. Affected entries carry only standard binding/key/field/value fields.

Redaction: default output runs the existing report redactor, so claim IDs remain structural but raw quote, numeric value, and observed surface data are placed only in affected key/value fields and become ordinal refs (redacted:ref:kN/redacted:ref:vN) or the existing keyed HMAC markers. --explicit is the only opt-in for raw details. Refusal text/details will omit raw claim/document content.

Not building now: HTML tag/entity normalization, PDF/DOCX extraction, fuzzy or semantic matching, document-wide quote search when byte_span is absent, currency conversion, multiple competing source versions, a new report schema or BindingKind, DuckDB integration, and any version bump. Real SEC/XML fixture coverage will include one true quote, fabricated quote, one-byte-off span, and a wrong-scale negative for the implemented checks.

comments.text:
Design before coding for bd-g49.1:

- Keep the existing pure-Rust engine and add a hand-written HTML normalizer; no new crate. It tokenizes comments, tags, and text. HTML comments are dropped. Script/style elements are dropped with their complete contents, case-insensitively. Other tags are dropped while their text content remains.

title: Reject unknown constraint fields without untagged fallback
description:
SAFETY BUG. The JSON schema already uses additionalProperties=false, but compile, validate, and run deserialize through Rust domain types without first enforcing that schema. The fix must make every constraint ingestion path enforce the same closed-world shape as verify.constraint.v1, including scalar-only predicate literals, without fallback through permissive untagged variants.

Scope is strict parsing and compilation only. Preserve all valid verify.constraint.v1 artifacts and existing scalar predicate literals. Do not add binding-qualified references or any new predicate semantics here.

title: Fix verify --lock to support canonical lock.v0 (bytes_hash with blake3: and sha256:)
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `crates/verify-duckdb/src/lock_check.rs:12-24` hardcodes `LOCK_VERSION = "lock.input.v1"` and parses `content_hash`.
- `crates/verify-duckdb/src/lock_check.rs:225-233` only computes `sha256:` digests.

## Impact
Real `cmdrvl/lock` manifests emit `version: "lock.v0"` with `bytes_hash` prefixed by `blake3:` or `sha256:`. As a result, `verify --lock` rejects every real lockfile produced by `hashbytes | lock` in the spine.

## Fix
1. Parse canonical `lock.v0` manifests (`members[].bytes_hash` and `members[].path`) and dispatch verification on `blake3:` and `sha256:` prefixes (refusing unknown algorithms deterministically).
2. Retain optional backward compatibility for legacy `lock.input.v1` only if required by existing fixtures, clearly marked deprecated.
acceptance_criteria:
- `verify run --lock` verifies real `cmdrvl/lock` `lock.v0` manifests using both `blake3:` and `sha256:` `bytes_hash` values.
- Tampered input bytes or unknown hash algorithm prefixes produce deterministic `E_LOCK_*` refusals.
- Unit and integration tests cover `lock.v0` (`blake3:` and `sha256:`) pass and drift/mismatch cases.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator on an exact git-archive export of origin/main 97a0cb9 (not a live tree), built in verify's own target with the pane's environment (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=3, no DuckDB rebuild). cargo test --locked -p verify-cli -p verify-duckdb --no-fail-fast: verify-cli bin 80, binding_qualified_determinism 3 / predicates 5 / refusals 5, cli 37, determinism 2, doctor 11, family_contract 11, golden_rules 22, perf_smoke 5, portable_rules 10, redaction 7, refusals 8; verify-duckdb lib 59, lock_integration 8, query_rules 7; 0 failed, 0 ignored. Not run: verify-core schema_contract, verify-engine embedding_equivalence, clippy, ubs. Own checks on a snapshot binary with my own lock files: sha256: lock and blake3: lock over the same csv are accepted (no refusal); a blake3 lock with the wrong digest, a one-byte-appended file, and an uppercase-hex sha256 lock each refuse E_INPUT_DRIFT exit 2; md5: prefix and a bare unprefixed hash refuse E_IO exit 2. Reconciliation (disclosed by the pane, accepted): the bead says E_LOCK_* codes but no such codes exist in verify, so existing E_INPUT_DRIFT/E_IO are used; also benchmark returns E_UNSUPPORTED_HASH_ALGORITHM for md5 where verify returns E_IO (family inconsistency, not a blocker). Flake: the pane's one unreproduced failure of its CLI lock test is documented in a bd-pnr comment (likely a killed child under load, unproven); test not deleted or ignored. NOT verified: multi-member locks, a flake loop result in this close (pane's loop result not seen by me).

title: Add default redaction and --explicit flag for verify failing-row output
description:
## Evidence (Source Audit)
- `crates/verify-duckdb/src/query_rules.rs:242-258` and `crates/verify-cli/src/run.rs:27-41` unconditionally serialize raw `AffectedEntry` fields (`key__*` and raw cell `value`) to stdout JSON on rule failure.

## Risk
Under `veil` zero-retention execution, an authorized `verify` run with a crafted failing rule (e.g., `SELECT *` failing every row) leaks raw sensitive cell contents directly into model context.

## Fix
1. Make redacted output the default: omit or hash raw `key__*` and cell `value` contents, emitting only rule IDs, failing row counts, column/binding identifiers, and opaque deterministic row/key hashes.
2. Add an explicit opt-in `--explicit` flag to include raw failing keys/values.
3. Declare `--explicit` in `operator.json` so `veil` can block raw-value disclosure under protected profiles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default `verify run` output contains zero raw cell or key values from bound inputs.
- `--explicit` restores raw `AffectedEntry` values when explicitly authorized.
- Canary-leak regression test plants sentinel values in bound inputs and asserts zero leakage in default stdout/stderr.
close_reason: Verified by orchestrator on the same exact export of 02376f5 (see bd-16h; same suites, all passing, incl tests/cli.rs 36 which contains failing_rows_are_redacted_by_default_and_raw_only_with_explicit and sql_error_text_that_quotes_a_cell_is_redacted_by_default). Independent canary through the built binary with MY OWN planted values (key ZQ-KEY-7001/7002, address ZQ-ADDR-CANARY-1/2) using a query rule returning key__property_id and value columns: DEFAULT --json, DEFAULT human, and DEFAULT --sample-affected 1 each show ZERO canaries in stdout+stderr; --explicit json and --explicit human show all four (control: the test can see the data); default affected entries keep the shape {binding, key:{property_id:'redacted:sha256:<16 hex>'}, value:'redacted:sha256:<16 hex>'}; two default runs are byte-identical (reproducible); SQL error text is withheld by default (details withheld by default redaction; pass --explicit). Diff scan of 433732d: assertions added, none removed in tests/refusals.rs, determinism.rs, binding_qualified_*.rs beyond the expected redaction-driven updates (2+/1-, 2+, 7 lines). LIMITATION, stated plainly and documented by the pane in redact.rs and robot-docs: the token is the first 8 bytes (16 hex) of an UNSALTED SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the value, so a low-entropy value (status code, small integer, short name) is recoverable by dictionary guess; this is the same weakness class the operator decided to fix for decoding (bd-1pv: ordinal refs by default, opt-in keyed HMAC); whether verify should get the same treatment is an operator decision, not part of this bead's acceptance ('zero raw cell or key values'). Also not redacted by design: column/binding/rule names, rule SQL text, file paths, counts. NOT verified: other rule ops' failing-row output beyond query_zero_rows (the pane's tests cover the shared redaction path), witness records with --no-witness off, full workspace suite.

title: security: unkeyed binding content_hash lets small inputs be recovered from redacted reports (also in twinning)
description:
SECURITY. Covers twinning AND standalone verify. Found during bd-uk5d; deliberately not changed there. The operator approved filing it separately (comment on bd-uk5d, 2026-11-26) and was told it must be resolved before the "no unkeyed hash of content in default output" rule is claimed met.

WHERE. verify.report bindings.<name>.content_hash, present in default (redacted) output of both:
- twinning embedded verify: unkeyed, unsalted SHA-256 over the JSON of all rows of the bound relation (twinning-kernel verify_bridge.rs relation_content_hash).
- standalone verify: unkeyed, unsalted SHA-256 of the bound input file (verify-duckdb bindings.rs file_sha256). The same value is what verify compares against a lock.

RISK. The hash covers cells that default redaction hides. When the relation or file is small and the unknown part has few possible values, anyone holding the report can try candidates until the hash matches. The reports are made to be sealed and passed on.

Shown with synthetic data (one row, id and layout assumed known, one integer amount among 100,000 possibilities): both default reports printed the amount as redacted:ref:v1, and trying candidates against content_hash recovered 48213 exactly, from twinning (build of 6ee1f52) and from released verify 0.7.5.

LIMITS. The guess must reproduce every hashed byte, so more rows or high-entropy cells make it infeasible. Nothing was tried against a realistic large relation.

NEEDS A DECISION, not just a patch. For standalone verify the file hash is an identity that lock checking and pack consumers rely on (and lock.v0 already carries unkeyed member hashes of the same files), so removing or keying it has consequences for those. For twinning the relation hash identifies the twin state that was checked. Options include: key it with the redaction key when one is set and omit it otherwise; omit it from default output and keep it under --explicit; or document it as outside the rule.

title: Add zero-ceremony inline/ad-hoc rule check mode for quick agent verification
description:
## Background & Rationale
Today running `verify` requires authoring a YAML/SQL file and compiling or pointing `--rules` at it. While declared, versioned rule files are essential for production pipelines, agents doing exploratory or iterative data work frequently want to run 1-3 quick deterministic checks in one shell call (e.g. "is `loan_id` unique and non-null, and is `balance >= 0`?") without writing temp YAML files.

## Goal
Add an ergonomic inline check path (e.g. `verify check data.parquet --not-null loan_id --unique loan_id --expr 'balance >= 0' --json` or `--rule-inline ...`) that compiles internally to the exact same `verify.constraint.v1` representation and emits the exact same `verify.report.v1` output (plus optional `--emit-rules` to save the generated YAML/constraint file for promotion!).

## Testing
- Tests verifying inline mode produces identical `verify.report.v1` localization and exit codes as equivalent YAML-authored rules.
- Test `--emit-rules` round-trips cleanly through `verify compile` and `verify validate`.
acceptance_criteria: Agents can run ad-hoc constraint checks in one command without authoring YAML files, producing standard verify.report.v1 output and optional exportable rules.
